extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO (particularly those subject to Office of Enrollment and Discipline proceedings), OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary/resignation matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for an attorney's affidavit of resignation seeking exclusion on consent under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, and the related disciplinary rules and post-approval obligations. Covers what the affidavit must state, the disciplinary rules alleged, statutory authority, publication and compliance steps, and reinstatement presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit must show the respondent's consent is freely and voluntarily rendered; that the respondent is aware a disciplinary complaint is pending and the allegations against him; that the respondent is aware of the specific disciplinary rules alleged to have been violated; that the respondent understands that, for reinstatement purposes, the OED Director will conclusively presume the allegations true and that he could not have successfully defended against them; that the respondent has fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60; and that the respondent consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the Respondent's September 25, 2012 Affidavit of Resignation contains the enumerated acknowledgments and that the Director determined the affidavit complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a). The affidavit need not admit the allegations but must show awareness of them and awareness of consequences (including reinstatement presumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed incompetence to handle legal matter (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes handling a legal matter which the attorney knows or should know that he is not competent to handle without associating with another practitioner who is competent to handle it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the disciplinary rules alleged in the complaint as one of the bases for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting legal matters entrusted to the attorney (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes neglecting legal matters entrusted to the attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct included filing a client's trademark applications untimely, failing to respond to Office correspondence, and allowing applications to become abandoned—behaviors consistent with neglect under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to inform client of Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) and (b) via § 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes failing to inform a client of Office correspondence where (i) it could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) it is received by the attorney on behalf of a client, and (iii) a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances the client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint alleged the respondent did not inform the client about Office correspondence received in connection with trademark applications—an instance of violating this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint alleged false or misleading statements to the client about the status of trademark applications as the basis for this charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest — accepting employment affected by attorney's own interests (37 C.F.R. § 10.62)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes, except with the consent of a client after full disclosure, accepting employment if the exercise of the attorney's professional judgment on behalf of the client will be or reasonably may be affected by the attorney's own financial, business, property, or personal interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failure to obtain client consent after full disclosure before simultaneously representing the client and another client with whom the attorney had financial and business dealings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining proffered employment where independent judgment or differing interests at risk (37 C.F.R. § 10.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires that an attorney decline proffered employment if the exercise of the attorney's independent professional judgment on behalf of a client will be or is likely to be adversely affected by acceptance, or if it would likely involve representing differing interests, except where it is obvious the attorney can adequately represent each client and each client consents after full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to allege improper simultaneous representation and insufficient disclosure/consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to seek lawful objectives by available means (37 C.F.R. § 10.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes intentionally failing to seek the lawful objectives of a client through reasonably available means permitted by law and the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged in connection with not pursuing available measures to protect the client's trademark matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper withdrawal leading to foreseeable prejudice (37 C.F.R. § 10.40(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proscribes withdrawing from employment in a proceeding before the Office without permission from the Office and prior to taking reasonable steps to avoid foreseeable prejudice to the rights of the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as an alleged violation where withdrawal or actions may have prejudiced client rights in trademark matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority to approve resignation and exclude (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. § 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has authority under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 to approve affidavits of resignation and to exclude a respondent on consent from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes and regulations as the basis for approving the affidavit and ordering exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided Notice of Exclusion on Consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a model Notice of Exclusion on Consent detailing allegations and cited disciplinary rules; publication in the Reading Room and Official Gazette is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-approval compliance obligations (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58, 11.59, 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; and Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cited sections govern obligations after exclusion on consent and procedures for reinstatement; the affidavit/Final Order explicitly references them and the respondent's acknowledgement of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement presumption (procedural effect upon later reinstatement application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledged that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations set forth in the disciplinary complaint are true and (ii) the respondent could not have successfully defended himself against such allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit consequence the respondent accepted in the affidavit; it affects the standard/assessment on any future reinstatement application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint motion to dismiss pending disciplinary complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall jointly move the hearing officer to dismiss the pending disciplinary complaint within 14 days of the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the parties to move to dismiss the complaint promptly after approval of the affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies that each party bears its own costs; no affirmative award of costs between parties is ordered.
